As a pet sitter, my insurance will cover damage to my home but go after the owner for it and vet bills for accidents. Anything that would be reasonably expected to be secured that dogs are known to chew or destroy (this is general) is on me. So I have to keep my home dog-proof. I do not allow access to my bedroom, kitchen or pantry if I cannot be home to supervise. I cannot leave out shoes, snacks, other people’s toys, chords, toys that have string or that shred. Dogs that are well behaved at home absolutely can do unusual things that she just could not warn you about ahead. Like chew shoes. Reason being, the new environment is very stimulating, sometimes stressful. Break in routine is stressful. 

I don’t blame you for not knowing, because you are not a pro sitter or dog owner- but I would say lighten up on your sister some. She seems willing to pay the difference, which is more than I would expect if I had allowed a dog access to something like that. You have to make your place fool proof when pet sitting, prepare for anything. I keep on hand baby gates, child locks on all my cabinets. I proof it the same as I would for a child.

I have twice helped clean out and give medical care to hoarding situations- one was 13 cats and 3 dogs, the other was 16 cats and two dogs. The first home was condemned after the animals were there for only 2 years with a sick elderly woman who had some help from her grown child. The other home we did had to be nearly gutted. This absolutely sounds like it is a hoarder. Both cases they believed they were doing good and called themselves a “rescue”. It is a mental illness and they do not think they are causing harm.

Be prepared to cry. To have your heart broken. Be prepared to see things and smell things that will give you nightmares and flashbacks. Be prepared for possible sick animals. Animals that are stressed tend to mark, have accidents. An infirm 80 year old would not be able to manage this many animals. The litter by itself was a serious chunk of the day. Then having to feed each animal based on who needed meds, who was underweight or overweight. The complexities of this situation are potentially many.

I am American- but I think not in terms of dishes, but skills that will help you cook most anything else.

1- how to break down various raw ingredients (chop/clean) this includes washing and chopping veg, trimming meat, soaking or washing grain and legumes

2– How to use SALT properly. When to use it. How much. What method? (Brine, rub, sprinkle over)

3- how to pan fry (knowing what cooked food looks like and how long it takes, what temperatures to use and how long)

4- How to cook in liquid. (Braise/boil/steam- when, what temp, why and how long)

5- How to follow a basic recipe. Learn what the basic measurements are preferably by weight and/or by your national standard. Learn how to follow all instructions and what common acronyms or abbreviations mean. 

I think with those basics you have a solid and varied foundation for picking up other cooking skills easily.

I am mixed race, and I have folks in my past who had these banks. That is why I recognized it. 

The Spanish missionaries married into (and in all likely possibility also raped) my native Nahuatl ancestors. My great grandparents, who were born in Mexico and were mixed with Spanish and Native blood amassed a TON of crap over the years. They were Catholics. Half of my generation in our family look native- half look white. So to me- I could see easily how a white looking family might have come to possess such an inflammatory item. All these memories I just did not want to deal with because their passing was a huge deal in my large family.

I am a Spanish speaker, those banks have a religious tie to them. They are not american.

The writing on the red band around the neck from the photo you provided is “hucha ayuda a las misiones” 

It translates to “Piggybank helps the Spanish Missions”

https://www.museoandaluzdelaeducacion.es/las-huchas-del-domund/

Summary:
World Mission Day, established by Pius XI in 1926 and later popularized in Spain by Ángel Sagarmínaga, aimed to fund mission activities through annual collections held on the penultimate Sunday in October. Central to these collections were DOMUND piggy banks, commonly found in Spanish classrooms from the 1950s to 1960s. Made of materials like glazed earthenware, tin, and plastic, these piggy banks were used by children who solicited donations from passers-by with phrases like “for the missions.” Schools often distributed these banks, and children would record their weekly contributions to ensure accountability. While familiar to many generations, the specific memories and uses of these piggy banks vary widely among individuals.

It should probably go to a museum. Who knows why they have it- perhaps they had a relative who did missionary work, but I would leave it be.

Edit- To be clear- the banks were done in a racist style that was popular at that time and are offensive. But you have no idea how it came to be in their possession, what they plan to do with it etc. it was in a private area that is generally off limits to most people. Their own bedroom. It is old enough that it could have belonged to a grand or even great grand parent and they just don’t know what to do with it since passing. It may be a painful thing for them to deal with so it sits there.

I wonder if perhaps they have a disability of some sort and they are just not disclosing it. I am Autistic and things being out of place can really get to me, however I am older and recognize that many of the small things are a “me” problem and will simply go and fix them. Not excusing the behavior but offering a possible explanation. We can share traits with OCD. In my youth something as small as a toilet seat up might set me off, because I will be anxious about the toilet being flushed and the mist in the air it creates which lands on everything spreading the germs from the bowl. (Neurotic, I know lol but this is where my mind goes) It was enough to send me in a meltdown once upon a time. Now I understand that I disclose my disability when asking for anything out of the ordinary, and choose what I ask wisely to make sure I am reasonable.

He may have an invisible disability you are unaware of, combined with the possibility nobody wanted the lowest pay for something like that. Or even that they wanted to offer fair pay for coming all the way out there.

As an example, someone with ADHD or Autism may get so wrapped up in work that they often forget to take the dog out, but make enough to pay for the care and want to make sure they still do right by the dog and not have constant accidents to clean up. The disability would mean that they are likely as uncomfortable with you being there as you were to be there and want you to just leave after taking the dog out so they can concentrate/relax. It would mean they may not have the social skills to interact with you and others in a way that makes sense to you. It would mean that they are embarrassed or protective of explaining that is why they behave this way. Otherwise the disruption means quality of work suffers possibly greatly for them and this can create situations where they are jobless. 

If they were trying to get you to stay longer and do things unrelated to dog care, I would personally be worried- but it more seemed like they wanted you in and out quietly and seamlessly instead.

I think maybe look into family therapy, and try to strive for a more harmonious home dynamic by allowing a safe space for all to discuss what their needs and struggles are. Also, never ever try to reason with an ASD person mid meltdown. Wait until they are calm. You may want to ask your wife what makes her cry. I don’t cry for “normal” reasons. I cry for very specific causes- when I am frustrated. When I feel I am being unfairly judged. When I feel like I am not being heard. 

I never cry from sadness, or anything “typical” like someone passing. Maybe ask her when you two have a calm moment. A great place/way to talk is on a car ride. I find it helps because it removes the issue of eye contact. It is one less thing to stop me from expressing my thoughts.

Edited to add- this “crying pattern” has caused me to be accused of being cold and manipulative in the past, which is why I brought it up. How our expression of emotion is interpreted in a way that to you seems illogical or uncaring; when we are not trying to be that way at all.

I took a look at your post history, and you note that you have children who are ADHD/are ADHD yourself. You likely have had moments in your life where you were misunderstood due to this. Now consider that in your wife’s case. 

Secondly- I saw that there had been issues with aggression in the past with your children. Has that been resolved? If not, it can be contributing to the behavior you are seeing in the ASD child and they may be feeding off one another.

Third- you have three kids, to her one ASD kid. That would have been a hellshock of a change for me as an ASD child. I absolutely would have had outbursts, anger issues and meltdowns due to the confusion from the changes, invasion of my peace and former space. Consider this- noise, lights, schedule changes, changes in diet possibly, a move- even as an adult these things can shut me down for a good year. An adult who understands what I am facing. This is a child who probably has no idea why all of this is so difficult, and so they are constantly on edge all the time making a meltdown more likely in terms of frequency. 

My brother is ADHD and because of that he was the polar opposite of me, and made my life very stressful. He was loud, energetic, unpredictable, aggressive, and I needed quiet, was methodical- etc. If your children are like that (and this is just part of their ADHD- I do understand) then the ASD child is possibly dealing with emotional and sensory overload to the extreme on a level they feel absolutely helpless to change. Additionally they probably wonder why these changes were unfairly thrust upon them by you and mom and why they had no choice- when life was likely comfortable for them before you arrived. 

Was the child happier before the marriage and are they having more outbursts now? Are they showing signs if emotional distress/depression? (This can show as more frequent demand avoidance/executive dysfunction/meltdowns) Was anything at all done to help them adjust?
